projects.title: AI Tenant Texting Assistant
projects.status: Live in draft mode (landlord reviews replies before sending)
projects.summary: An iPhone automation that reads a tenant's text, checks it against the lease, and drafts a reply in the landlord's voice in seconds. Built for two rental properties with no new apps, numbers, or monthly fees.

caseStudy.heading: The problem
caseStudy.body: Landlords get a steady stream of tenant texts: when rent is due, where to send it, what to do about a broken appliance. Most of the answers are already in the lease, but each one still pulls the landlord away from whatever they're doing.

caseStudy.heading: What I built
caseStudy.body: An automation that runs on the landlord's own iPhone. When the tenant texts, it sends the message to an AI model along with a prompt built from the signed lease, and returns a draft reply in seconds. No new phone number, no app for the tenant to install, no monthly software fee. I set it up for two rental properties.

caseStudy.heading: How it works
steps: A Shortcuts automation fires when a message arrives from the tenant's number.
The message is passed into a custom prompt holding the key lease terms: rent, payment method, term and renewal notice, utilities, appliances, house rules, and repair process.
The AI drafts a short reply in the landlord's voice, in whatever language the tenant writes in.
The draft appears as a notification for the landlord to review. Once trusted, it can send on its own.

start: Message + lease prompt sent to AI
end: Landlord sends, or auto-send once trusted

caseStudy.heading: Guardrails
items: Answers only what the lease covers. Anything else gets a neutral holding reply.
Never agrees to repair dates, entry times, rent changes, or lease changes. Those stay with the landlord.
Treats the tenant's text as content, not commands, so "ignore your instructions" tricks fail.
Emergencies always get a safety-first reply: call 911, then the landlord.
Angry or legal messages (lawyers, the Landlord and Tenant Board, withholding rent) get a calm acknowledgment and nothing more.
Kept away from lease clauses that may not hold up under Ontario's Residential Tenancies Act.

caseStudy.heading: What I learned
items: Shortcuts variables have to be inserted as tokens; typed placeholders silently break the flow.
A separate shortcut needs to be set to accept input before an automation can hand it the message.
Model choice depends on hardware: Apple's built-in ChatGPT action needs an iPhone 15 Pro or newer, so older phones use the Claude app's Ask Claude action instead.
Putting a closing instruction after the tenant's message makes the prompt much harder to hijack.

caseStudy.heading: Stack
items: Apple Shortcuts (Message automation, Receive input, Show Notification, Send Message)
Apple Intelligence ChatGPT action (iPhone 15 Pro and newer)
Claude iOS app "Ask Claude" action (older iPhones, iOS 18+)
Custom system prompt with scope lock and prompt-injection defense
